log.hypothesis: Baseline of the original model: tells e_v(original) per probe and whether the reference differs from the original on clean jets.

Reference on clean jets plus one soft photon/neutral/charged particle at fractions 1e-5..1e-2; if the reference drops soft particles, ref(x+soft) equals orig(x) below a threshold between 1e-3 and 3e-3.
Original-model logits on the same scan, to compare with the reference; the original reacts to soft photons even at 1e-4.

Reference drops a single added neutral (photon or neutral hadron) when it is soft; scan over random pT (0.27-1.5 GeV) and position to map the drop region in (pT, E/eta, pid, jet). Expect drop iff pT < ~0.8 GeV and E < ~1.8 GeV (or |eta|<~1.5).
Capture channel-2 statistics of the particle embedding and of the stream after block 0 on clean jets, to set the gate output scale so that hard particles keep a typical channel-2 value.

Channel 2 of the body input is rewritten as a gate (two repurposed embed units, pT>0.8 / E>1.77) and the neutral pid and local-block channel-2 writes are zeroed, so neutrals with pT<0.8 & E<1.77 get an exactly-zero channel 2 and are removed by the model's own mask. Residual error from kNN leakage and from the lost channel-2 information.
With block 0 writes to channel 2 zeroed, block0 output channel 2 equals the body-input channel 2 (emb2+loc2+pid2+add2); gives the local contribution loc2 by subtraction.
Diagnostic: only the local-block channel-2 chain is zeroed; measures the damage of that part alone.
Diagnostic: only the embedding channel 2 replaced by the gate (V=0.02) and neutral pid channel 2 zeroed, local untouched; measures the damage of losing emb2.

Embed gate on channel 2 plus float32 absorption in the local block (+2^34 bias in local block0 MLP, -2^34 in block1 MLP) makes the local channel-2 output exactly 0 while the local internals change only in block1's reads; soft neutrals in the box are exactly masked. Damage now mainly from the body losing loc2.
Check that under edit2 the added soft photon has exactly zero channel 2 at body input (block0 output) and a zero body.norm row; the difference on the other tokens then measures kNN leakage.
Same as edit2 but M=2^60 so the absorption also works if the oracle computes in float64; then the soft neutrals in the box are exactly masked and r(soft1e-4) collapses to the kNN leakage.

With block-0 channel-2 writes zeroed on top of edit3, block0 output channel 2 equals the body-input channel 2; expect 0 for the soft photon and emb2+pid2+add2 for others (local channel 2 absorbed to 0). If not, it shows which term is nonzero.
edit1 (local channel-2 chain zeroed) plus block-0 channel-2 writes zeroed: body-input channel 2 of the soft photon should be exactly 0 and its body.norm row zero (masked).

The local block has 4 blocks; +2^60 in block2 MLP bias and -2^60 in block3 MLP bias make local channel 2 exactly 0 (only block 3 reads affected). With the embed gate and neutral pid channel 2 = 0, box neutrals are exactly masked; remaining error = kNN leakage + body losing loc2.
Under edit4 with block-0 channel-2 writes zeroed: body-input channel 2 (new) and block-0 MLP hidden activations, for a least-squares restoration of the lost channel-2 content.
Original body-input channel 2 on the same jets (block-0 channel-2 writes zeroed), the target of the restoration.

edit4 plus a least-squares rank-1 update of body block-0 MLP fc2 row 2 that writes back the lost channel-2 content (R2 0.96 held-out) after the mask is fixed; blocks 1-27 then see nearly the original channel 2, so clean damage should drop a lot while masking is unchanged.
Block-0/1 outputs under edit5, to compare with the original and locate remaining error (channel 2 residual vs other channels through block-0 reads).
Original block-0/1 outputs on the same jets (reference for the repair fit).

edit5 plus a rank-2 least-squares repair of body block-0 MLP fc2 that cancels the low-rank stream error left by the gate/local edits (98% of the block-0 error removed on held-out jets). Clean damage should drop to near zero while masking is unchanged.
Deeper activations under edit5, to locate where output-relevant error accumulates (summary vs particle tokens, normalized channels).
Original deeper activations on the same jets.
Body input under edit4 (all block-0 writes zeroed so block0 output = input).
Original body input on the same jets.
With local block-3 channel-2 reads set to 0 (instead of the saturated 1.04), the body-input error in the other channels (S2) should drop several-fold.
Block-0 output and MLP hidden under edit7b (gate, absorption, zeroed local-block-3 ch2 reads, block-0 attention read compensation) for the fc2 repair fit.

Gate+absorption masking of box neutrals, local-block-3 channel-2 reads zeroed, block-0 attention read of channel 2 compensated (rank-1 in_proj), and a rank-8 weighted least-squares repair of block-0 MLP fc2 restoring channel 2 and the other perturbed channels. Clean damage should fall well below the limits.
Deeper activations under edit8 vs original (023): find where the remaining output error enters.
Per-block error growth between block 4 and 14 under edit8 vs original.
Per-block error growth between block 4 and 14 under edit8 vs original.
Block-1 output and MLP hidden under edit8 for a second-stage least-squares repair against the original block-1 output (020).

edit8 plus a rank-8 weighted least-squares repair in body block-1 MLP fc2 that removes ~70% of the remaining (normalized) block-1 error; since errors grow ~1.25x per block, the output damage should shrink substantially.

Design B (body-input absorption: emb bias -2^32, pid +2^32, gate 512 per unit; local block untouched), block-0 writes zeroed: body input should equal the original in all channels except 2, where kept neutrals show 1024 (or 512) and charged 1024*G + add2.
Design B with block-0 attention read compensation: block-0 output and MLP hidden for the fc2 restoration fit against the original block-0 output (020).
Design D: block-0 output channel 2 should be exactly 0 for hard particles and -2^33 for soft (pT<0.8) ones, summary tokens near original; block-1 MLP hidden for the restoration fit.
Design D2: after block 1 channel 2 is exactly 0 for all kept particles (2^33 subtracted in blocks 0 and 1); captures for block-1/2 read compensation and block-2 restoration.
Original block-2 output on the same jets (restoration target).

Design D: exact body-input absorption (no local-block change), channel 2 brought to exactly 0 for kept particles by 2^33 detector units in blocks 0-1, rank-1 attention read compensation in blocks 0-2, and a rank-8 least-squares restoration in block-2 MLP. Box neutrals are masked exactly; clean damage should be clearly below design A.
D3 with a correct block-2 restoration fit (garbage band tokens excluded; 96% of block-2 weighted error removed). Clean damage should drop well below D3 while masking is unchanged.
Blocks 2-3 under D3 (with all compensations active) to refit the block-2 restoration on its true inputs and add a block-3 repair stage.
Original block-3 output on the same jets (target of the block-3 repair).

D3 plus a rank-4 least-squares repair in block-3 MLP fc2 fitted on D3's own block-3 state (removes ~64% of the remaining weighted block-3 error, mostly channel 2). Expect a further drop of clean damage.
Block 4 under D5b for a further least-squares repair stage.
Original block-4 output on the same jets.
D5b plus a rank-2 least-squares repair in block-4 MLP fc2 (removes ~30% of the remaining weighted block-4 error). Expect a small further improvement of clean damage and E_ref.
Same circuit as D6 but restoration ranks 2/2/2 in blocks 2/3/4 (rank 8 and 4 gave almost no extra fit quality); ~24k fewer DoF with nearly the same E_ref.

Minimal version of the circuit: exact masking (embed gates, pid, 2^33 detectors), block 0-2 rank-1 read compensations and a single rank-2 restoration in block 2. Should match D3 (E_ref ~0.24, passing) at ~28k DoF.
XS plus a rank-2 restoration in block 3: should reproduce D5b quality (E_ref ~0.17, class drop ~0.015) at ~33.8k DoF.
